title: Classification Needs a Ready Runtime
description: I am making local classification ask whether its required runtime profile is ready before it accepts work. A listening endpoint is not the right model.
body:
A reachable local-model endpoint is not enough evidence that classification is ready to run. VALESKA’s classifier has a particular dependency: the expected model must be selected, loaded, and available with enough GPU memory before a request is sent. Today I finish pointing that preflight at the standalone GPU arbiter. The claim is not that every local model will now start. The claim is that the classifier can ask whether its required runtime profile is ready and decline when it is not.

The wrong default

The usual move is to probe a port, hear an answer, and treat whatever is listening as the right model. Something is up. That is not the same as the named profile being loaded, the required VRAM being reserved, or a competing task having left the runtime alone. Those are operating facts. The classifier should not guess them.

You do not send a train onto a track because the station lights are on. You ask whether this train, on this track, with this clearance, is ready. I am putting that question in front of classification.

Yesterday’s helper, today’s placement

Yesterday I added the Valeska-side helper so the AI classifier, the training scorer, and the training-dataset generator can request a named runtime profile before they use local inference. The helper reads a classification profile setting and offers explicit controls for the profile, a required-runtime mode, and bypassing the preflight when that is appropriate for a defined environment. If the runtime manager reports that the profile is not ready, the classifier records the failure and does not proceed as though the model had been verified.

Today I point that helper at the standalone GPU arbiter repository. Model selection, VRAM claims, loading through LM Studio, and release behavior belong to the arbiter’s profile-based manager. I am not recreating them inside VALESKA. The profile named for repository classification identifies the intended model configuration. The classifier remains responsible for deciding whether to classify; the arbiter owns the runtime preparation request. Separating those jobs makes the dependency easier to inspect when classification is unavailable.

What this does and does not establish

I now have a gating path. Before it contacts a local model, the classifier can call the runtime helper and receive either readiness information or a reason to disable the operation. Batch-oriented callers get the same route, so training work does not silently use a different local state from interactive classification. Local inference is shared infrastructure. Its limits are affected by model size, VRAM, startup state, and other consumers.

This does not establish that the named profile can always be loaded on this machine, that every VRAM claim will be granted, or that a classification result is accurate. Those are separate questions. A ready runtime is a precondition for classification, not proof of the quality of the classification itself. A clean failure from the preflight is better than an unsupported claim that a model was ready.

The next test

The next test is to exercise the actual profile under the shared GPU conditions it will face in use. The check should show the selected profile, the availability result, and the classifier’s behavior in both paths: classify only after successful preparation, and remain disabled with an understandable record when preparation fails. The same test should run through a batch caller, because the shared contract is the point of the change. Results from that operational test belong in a later entry. Today’s evidence is the preflight integration and its transfer to the arbiter-managed runtime.

Historical basis: VALESKA commits 346b2d9 (May 16) and 75e0ba4 (May 17, 2026). The article is dated to the 17th, when the helper was pointed at the arbiter.

data.coverAlt: A workshop instrument asking a distant glass tower whether the named runtime is ready before work is sent down the line: classification gated on a profile, not on a listening port.
